editorial:
Imagine you are a high school student in the early 2000s when the internet was still a wild place. You and your friends stumble upon a disturbing murder video online, but instead of running away, you decide to play detective. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow a group of girls who refuse to believe the video is real, leading them into a dangerous game of cat and mouse. The vibe is very much like those classic J-Horror movies where the school hallways feel creepy and every corner could hide something scary. Since the cast is full of young idols, you get a lot of energy and a feeling of youth mixed with pure terror.

What really works is how the movie keeps you guessing about who the killer is. The pacing is quick, and the scares hit when you least expect them. Some of the acting is a bit over-the-top, but that actually fits the style of the era. If you love old-school slasher flicks, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The story ends with a shocking twist where you find out the killer was hiding in plain sight. After a brutal chase through the school, the main characters realize the murder videos were a sick game. Most of the girls do not make it, as the killer picks them off one by one. The final scenes show the cycle of violence continuing, leaving you with a grim feeling that the horror is not truly over for everyone.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves early 2000s Japanese horror and slasher movies.
